articles.body: KENOSHA, Wisconsin —   The progressive movement’s midterms march has arrived in Wisconsin, where a democratic socialist is forcing establishment Democrats to mount an all-out, last-ditch effort to stop her. State Rep. Francesca Hong is the front-runner to become the Democratic gubernatorial nominee, fueled by a populist campaign tapping into voters’ cost of living concerns. David Crowley, the Milwaukee County Executive backed by outgoing Gov. Tony Evers, has emerged as the top candidate trying to cut off Hong’s bid. Ahead of Tuesday’s primary, electability was top of mind for voters and both candidates as they raced to prove they could build the widest, strongest coalition against presumptive Republican nominee Tom Tiffany. Crowley and Evers have been barnstorming the swing state over the past week, warning a vote for Hong risks losing the governor’s mansion in November to Tiffany, a hard-right member of the House Freedom Caucus backed by President Donald Trump. “You know, it's the only time that I know that the governor — Tony Evers — the Republican Governors Association and Turning Point USA have ever been on the same page: in thinking that Francesca Hong is the best candidate to lose this race,” Crowley said in an interview at a local tavern in Sheboygan on Friday. Hong rejects those warnings. Speaking to voters at events across the state, Hong argues Democratic voters are fed up with the establishment ahead of November — and that she can appeal to a wide array of Democrats, Republicans and people who don’t feel represented by either party. “We have to take this moment, a movement moment, and be bold with transformative change, and build the actual big tent that we can and we must be as Democrats,” Hong told a crowd of about 50 people gathered at a senior community center in deep-red Siren. Hong, a 37-year-old former chef and single mother who represents the bluest district in the state assembly, has charted a remarkably rapid rise in a purple state that Trump won by just shy of 30,000 votes in 2024. She launched her campaign as a long shot, with far less name recognition than other Democrats in the race like Lt. Gov. Sara Rodriguez and former Lt. Gov. Mandela Barnes. Both of them have since dropped out . And despite being at a consistent fundraising disadvantage — Hong still has not put out a single television ad — the progressive has maintained wide leads in public polling. But Hong’s campaign has also faced intense scrutiny over a string of controversial past social media posts, including advocating for defunding the police and railing against Thanksgiving . She was later slammed for being unable to give a straightforward answer to CNN about whether she would “cancel Thanksgiving.” Following those missteps, Hong's team has clamped down on her interactions with both local and national media at campaign events in the final stretch. She has also moderated some of her past positions in public remarks, emphasizing repeatedly that she is “serious about public safety” and even attempting to eschew some of her anti-establishment ties. On Wednesday, she reversed herself on Thanksgiving, telling POLITICO that it was, in fact, her favorite holiday. And asked by POLITICO on Saturday if she had any regrets about her past, she told reporters at a campaign stop in Sheboygan that she had learned from her tweets. “I had some hot takes, some bad takes on Twitter, but when you're a business owner running a restaurant during Covid, trying to pay bills as a student, you're putting feelings out there into the world,” Hong said. “But I've evolved, I've learned. I think it's more dishonest not to learn.” Hong has leaned heavily into affordability policies, including raising the state’s minimum wage from $7.25 to $20, progressive taxation and a statewide one-year moratorium on data center construction — a salient issue in Wisconsin, where several local governments have already voted on moratoriums. “While many of our supporters or other folks have framed us as anti-establishment, what we are for is working-class people,” she told POLITICO. “It's not so much being anti-establishment as it is ensuring that we're listening to voters who are demanding change.” But many Democrats in the state worry her ideology — including the old social media posts hawking far-left talking points — will be a political risk in a battleground general election. Pro-Republican PACs, including one associated with the Republican Governors Association, have spent millions of dollars to boost Hong in the primary so they can face who they perceive to be a weaker candidate in November. Kyle Kilbourn, a Democrat who unsuccessfully ran against Tiffany for his House seat in 2024, said he still had not decided who to support in the primary because of concerns about “electability statewide.” “The last several elections have been very very close, by one or two percentage points, and so it matters,” he told POLITICO while attending a Hong event at a brewery in Rhinelander. Even some of Hong’s supporters are anxious. “It’s always going to be a concern,” Jan Stroman, who attended an event in River Falls, said when asked if Hong could win against Tiffany. Robert LaGesse, 74, said at an event in far-north Superior on Friday he was voting for Hong — but admitted Hong’s tweets about abolishing the police “sounds like a foolish statement that could hurt her big time.” At the same event, a young Hong campaign volunteer asked her about those social media posts.“I’m not going to abolish the police as governor,” Hong responded. “I cannot and I will not defund the police.” She was asked a similar version of the same question at nearly every other event last week. Some supporters also fear that Hong will face racist and sexist backlash as an Asian American woman. Wisconsin has never elected a governor who is not a white man. “There's a lot of sexism yet in our country,” Tim Freiss, 60 — a Hong supporter who previously voted for both Bush presidencies — said in an interview outside his home in Green Bay. “Honestly, what I'm worried about is her race, because our state is very racist,” another Hong supporter, Heidi Meyer, 48, said as Hong canvassed her neighborhood in Appleton. Democratic officials in the Badger State are determined to unify after the primary, but many are deeply concerned Hong isn’t running the disciplined campaign required to defeat a Trump-backed Republican in Wisconsin. The messy race has also deeply divided Democrats in the state. Hong’s allies bristle at Evers’ campaign against her, using his resources — including his own communications staff — to boost Crowley. Evers defeated Republican then-Gov. Scott Walker in 2018 by deploying his brand of more moderate Democratic policies to win over independents and limit deep losses in rural areas. But he decided not to run for a rare third term as governor. Evers on Friday would not commit to endorsing or campaigning with Hong should she win — though Democrats expect he’ll have to. “I want to have a chance to take a breath, and once that's in a position, we'll see,” Evers said in an interview as he walked with Crowley from a Hmong family-owned bakery in Sheboygan to the corner tavern packed with supporters. Crowley, asked if he would campaign for Hong this fall if she wins the nomination, shot back with a smile: “Ask her that too.” But he quickly added: “I want to be very clear: I'm not in this race running against any of my opponents. I'm running for the votes of Wisconsinites, and if they don't choose me to be the nominee, my job is to make sure that it's blue no matter who.” Asked Saturday if she would endorse and campaign with Crowley if he wins on Tuesday, Hong replied with one word: “Yes.” Hong has admitted the democratic socialist label comes with baggage — “I can't say I always love it for me,” she said at a restaurant in River Falls — but she also rejected the notion that her campaign is undisciplined and noted that establishment Democrats had consistently underestimated her bid. She hopes to work with Democrats across the ideological spectrum in the sprint toward November. “We’re a serious campaign that has built a movement and turned out new voters, folks who are voting for the first time,” Hong said. “We're a serious campaign that knows how to win, but we're also serious about working as a coalition and making sure that we collaborate and coordinate with the people that we need to to make sure we defeat Tom Tiffany in the fall.” Crowley has charted a more moderate path than Hong’s blistering democratic socialism. In an interview, he argued the party needs “someone who's not just going to fight back, but also who can sit at the negotiating table and be able to work with folks who want to deliver for those that we represent.” He also ruled out the data center moratorium popular with a wide swath of voters that Hong is running on and using to pull in some pockets of rural support: “So, the way I hear that question is that we're going to preempt local communities from not being able to focus on their own economic development,” Crowley said. There are signs that Crowley is making some gains. But he’s still 20 percentage points behind Hong in the latest polling . “Crowley is closing the gap, but it’s likely too little, too late,” said one longtime Wisconsin Democratic strategist, who was granted anonymity to candidly discuss the governor’s pick. Crowley’s team argues that Wisconsin polling is likely off just as it was in Michigan, where Abdul El-Sayed clinched the Democratic Senate nomination last week by a tighter than expected margin. But the signs of Hong’s strength are evident across the state, beyond just her stronghold of Madison. The first voter Crowley greeted at his opening Sheboygan stop Friday, Paige Gerber, said in an interview later she had already voted early for Hong. Supporters at the Crowley event later in the day were well aware of his standing. Voter after voter in interviews with POLITICO expressed alarm that their party was poised to pick Hong, a losing horse in their view. Retirees in “radicalized by basic decency” T-shirts sipped on beer and cheered when Evers walked through the door with Crowley, alongside local IBEW union workers and teachers. “Tony! Tony!” chants eventually rang through the bar. A Crowley staffer at one point tried to start a “David! David!” cheer. But it never caught on. Tyler Katzenberger contributed to this report.
articles.headline: Wisconsin’s Dem establishment is scrambling to stop a democratic socialist Tuesday

articles.body: South Carolina Republicans might be watching history repeat itself. A special election Senate primary on Tuesday, triggered by Sen. Lindsey Graham’s sudden death, has all the makings of their rollercoaster governor’s primary back in June: A front-runner endorsed by President Donald Trump but facing a steep uphill battle to consolidate the field behind her. And the looming threat of a runoff election that could lead to a late surge from another Republican. Darline Graham is running for a full term to replace her late brother, leading in some public polls over GOP Reps. Russell Fry and Ralph Norman, former Gov. Mark Sanford and businessman Mark Lynch. The crowded field makes it very unlikely she or anyone else will clinch the majority needed to avoid a bitter runoff. And, aside from deploying his standard playbook of a few Truth Social posts supporting Graham and a last-minute tele-rally scheduled for Monday, Trump has made no public indication of what else he is planning to do to help. For one particular South Carolina Republican, the situation is all too familiar: Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette had Trump’s backing in the GOP governor’s primary — and then lost to Alan Wilson in the runoff after he rose in the polls and secured a rare double endorsement from the president. Asked if she wished Trump would have done more to boost her, Evette told POLITICO: “Obviously, yes. I do wish that, but you know, it didn't happen that way.” She said she has not yet decided who to endorse in the Senate primary and is keeping a close eye on how it plays out. "Run it back," said one national GOP operative, granted anonymity to speak openly about how the South Carolina Senate primary may turn into a redux of the governor's race. "The long and short of it, [Graham’s] got a pretty low ceiling." The snap Senate election tees up another test of Trump’s influence over the Republican Party. It will reveal whether the president’s word alone is enough to carry his preferred candidate to the nomination, and the lengths to which he is willing to go to boost his picks — especially ones who find themselves with an uncertain path to victory. This will be Graham’s first ever contest at the ballot box in a state known for its bruising GOP political battles. Nearly half a dozen local Republican officials and strategists alike believe Graham is in a strong position to win the first round of voting. But whoever secures the second place spot will determine just how much more support she may need from Trump to overcome a one-on-one challenge. The White House didn’t respond to a request for comment. Republicans differed on whether Norman or Fry would pose the bigger challenge to Graham’s path to victory in a runoff scenario. Norman boasts a longtime base of conservative support in the state, while Fry, who was elected to Congress in 2022, is seen as an up-and-coming star who has caught Trump’s interest. “If it's Darline and Russell, it definitely has some flavors of the governor's race,” said Tyson Grinstead, an RNC committee member and chair of the Richland County GOP, who is staying neutral in the Senate race. Both candidates have good relationships with the president — and Trump has already proven he’s willing to double endorse in a runoff. However, Grinstead added, there are some key differences. The main flaw in Evette’s strategy that Republicans in South Carolina have pointed to was her decision to run too intensely on her ties to the president in lieu of a more issues-first message. “I think most of the criticism came because I got his endorsement, and everybody was fighting for his endorsement. That's how I looked at it,” Evette said in an interview, deflecting the criticism. “In states like this that have these runoffs, where very few people come out, I think if you're not tied into the establishment, I think it hurts you in some form of fashion.” With the president's endorsement already secured, Graham is making a clear effort to differentiate herself not only from her field of contenders, but from her brother as well. In an interview with Fox News announcing her run, Graham made a point to emphasize her intention to focus on domestic issues in contrast to the late senator’s foreign policy-hued legacy. And she brought the same focus to her first debate stage appearance last week. “If anybody understands the struggles of South Carolinians, it's me,” Graham said on stage last week, talking about her own cost of living struggles — even as she vowed to support Trump’s pet projects while in office, including the SAVE America Act. "Of course the campaign's advertising highlights the Trump endorsement. We're proud of it, and there's no question it's still the gold standard in Republican politics,” said a person familiar with Graham’s approach, granted anonymity to discuss internal campaign strategy. “But Darline knows an endorsement opens a door, it doesn't walk through it for you,” this person added. “She's out there every day earning this on her own, because that's what voters deserve — a candidate who shows up and makes her own case, not one who assumes the race is already won." One of Graham’s key advantages in staving off a late upset lies in her inherited slate of seasoned operatives and statewide campaign infrastructure — a hallmark of Lindsey Graham’s decades of success in the state. “Lindsey's team has been the best team in South Carolina,” said Grinstead, who worked for the late senator’s campaigns in past cycles. “They're organized, they have a grassroots presence, they have field staff.” Still, Graham is likely to face a competitive runoff regardless of which candidate squeaks into second place. Fry and Norman are seen as the two most likely contenders based on limited public polling available in the race so far. In a glimpse of how fluid and unpredictable the primary has become, a straw poll conducted by the South Carolina Republican Party showed Graham in third place, trailing both Norman and Fry. The two representatives offer competing flavors for Republicans to choose from. Fry is seen in both Washington and Columbia as a rising star in the party. He also has a fan in Trump who, in the muddied political waters immediately following Lindsey Graham’s death, said in an interview with Newsmax that the House Republican is “outstanding” and a “very talented person.” But questions remain about the legal process of what happens to his congressional seat should he win his party’s nomination for Senate and go on to win in the general election. The state party has signaled they would act quickly to address a vacancy to protect House Republicans’ extremely narrow majority in Congress. Norman, for his part, already gave up his House seat to run for governor earlier this year. He is a longtime fixture of the state’s most conservative factions, who has at times been a thorn in Trump’s side, like when he endorsed former U.N. Ambassador Nikki Haley for president in 2024. But he’s seen as the standard bearer for the powerful Freedom Caucus’ ultraconservative politics in the state, and his gubernatorial bid has left him with a statewide operation that he can reactivate in his run for Senate. Graham, Fry, and Norman all declined to comment. Both of Graham’s likely top opponents have honed most of their fire on each other — one of the clearest signs that the first round of the primary is shaping up to be a battle for second place. Still, Graham’s allies have lobbed their own attacks against Fry. Security in Strength, a PAC that once supported Lindsey Graham’s 2024 reelection, is up on TV with an ad that shows an AI-depiction of Fry’s likeness transposed onto a slice of meat in a frying pan, dumped out by Trump with the words “REJECTED” splashed across the screen. Fry has recently started taking aim at Graham, launching an ad claiming that she “ballooned the size” and doubled the spending of a government agency — but did not specify which. Graham has worked for the South Carolina Vocational Rehabilitation Department and has led the Commission for the Blind since 2019. “If Russell Fry wants to attack Senator Darline for helping people with disabilities find jobs and live independently, that's a bold fight to pick,” Abby Zilch, a Graham spokesperson, said in response in a post on social media.
articles.headline: Will Darline Graham face the same fate Pamela Evette did in South Carolina?

articles.body: Rhode Island Gov. Dan McKee has a month to turn around primary challenger Helena Foulkes’ 20-point lead or become the first sitting U.S. governor to lose a primary in eight years. The race represents another crest in the world’s post-pandemic anti-incumbent wave, which has transcended ideological lines as voters express broad frustration with high costs of living and governments they don’t feel are working for them. It’s a throughline from insurgent progressive victories to Kamala Harris’ 2024 loss to President Donald Trump’s growing unpopularity. And it’s all down to a bridge. Signs outside Rhode Island’s partially closed Washington Bridge tell drivers: “Thank you for your patience.” But voters who’ve lived through the resulting traffic crisis since emergency safety concerns emerged in 2023 keep telling Foulkes the messages make them feel the opposite. Despite some improvement, they’re fed up with commuting and economic troubles stemming from the bridge’s slowdown. One older woman told Foulkes she wanted to take out her BB gun and shoot the signs. The contest is a rematch of the 2022 primary, when McKee (who’d been elevated to governor when Gina Raimondo became Commerce secretary) narrowly edged out Foulkes in a multi-candidate race. The primary doesn’t fall neatly along the ideological lines that have riven Democrats elsewhere. Foulkes and McKee, both baby boomers, have positioned themselves as relatively mainstream, center-left Dems. “I’m running against people’s belief that the status quo is maybe just as good as we’re ever going to be,” Foulkes told Playbook. She’s proposed funding 20,000 new housing units with a millionaires tax. “It’s so important that people feel a sense of momentum and energy … because I think oftentimes government doesn’t feel urgent to people, and their lives are really hurting.” Rhode Island is small enough — an hour’s drive from one corner to the other — that a single bridge symbolizes the trend. (The Washington Bridge is a key conduit between Providence and East Providence.) Almost everybody says the bridge is the No. 1 issue in the race and voters’ perception of McKee’s tenure. He and Foulkes have squabbled over the pace of rebuilding, the bidding process and the state Department of Transportation leadership. Residents are also struggling with some of the country’s highest electric rates and worst housing affordability metrics. The state’s anti-establishment/outsider energy isn’t limited to this contest. In the GOP gubernatorial primary, the polling leader is Elaine Pelino — a former actress, Howard Lutnick assistant and publisher of Tigress Magazine ( “For the Fierce, One of a Kind Woman” ) — who’s gathered steam with anti-socialism Facebook posts. For lieutenant governor, incumbent Democrat Sabina Matos faces strong challenges from Newport City Councilor Xay Khamsyvoravong and others. And Providence Mayor Brett Smiley is trying to fend off state Rep. David Morales on his left. But McKee is mounting a vigorous defense of his time in office, saying he’s delivered for Rhode Islanders — despite Trump’s obstacles — on jobs, SNAP, wind energy, education, hospitals, housing and energy. The governor argues he’s prioritized safety on the bridge after previous leaders kicked the can down the road. One recent poll by McKee allies found a closer race, with Foulkes ahead by just 6 points. “My record is going to really be the important factor,” McKee said in an interview. “My opponent’s record’s been in the corporate boardroom, really putting profits over people.” That’s the heart of McKee’s message, which banks on another crucial Democratic 2026 narrative carrying the day: a working people’s populism taking on the elite business class. McKee has long had a base of union support. In Foulkes, he has an opponent who’s no democratic socialist. She was a longtime CVS executive and comes from a storied political lineage (her grandfather and uncle, Thomas and Chris Dodd, were both senators). “It’s kind of a running bit here that her campaign is, in a very real way, being run from the deck of the Dunes Club in Narragansett,” said McKee campaign manager Drew Shannon, referring to the exclusive, members-only beach club. And McKee has gone negative on the airwaves, accusing Foulkes of cutting people’s health care and turning a blind eye to opioid addiction during her time at CVS. “She’s a denier: someone who denies the progress we’re making,” McKee told Playbook. “Just like she denies the role she played in fueling an opioid crisis.” Both candidates got fiery in a radio debate this week. As of July 31, Foulkes had five times McKee’s cash on hand. McKee has been rolling out a string of notable endorsements, many from labor, including teachers, firefighters, building trades and Planned Parenthood Votes! Rhode Island PAC. If he can pull off a comeback, it’ll likely be on the strength of union support. But his positioning as a labor champion from the working-class Blackstone Valley — the birthplace of the U.S.’ Industrial Revolution — has been partially undercut by high-profile defections in his base. The Rhode Island SEIU State Council backed Foulkes. The state Democratic Party and the state AFL-CIO voted not to endorse in the race, both of which were seen as big blows to McKee. “The labor movement is going to be in both camps,” AFL-CIO President Patrick Crowley said. And a number of Democratic city committees have sprung for Foulkes. Cumberland Mayor Jeff Mutter, who serves in the role McKee once held, is among those now supporting her. “There’s been some stances taken that I don’t think represent the same person who was a mentor of mine,” Mutter said of McKee, calling his endorsement a difficult personal choice. “It’s one of those times,” Mutter added, “where the advantage of incumbency might not be an advantage at this point because there’s just so much kind of frustration.” Like this content? articles.body: Michigan Democrats’ scramble to unify after a brutal primary continued Friday with a preplanned rally that brought together the statewide ticket. It also brought out Pete Buttigieg, a former and potentially future presidential candidate, whose presence helped underscore the stakes not just in November, but for 2028. Holding the Michigan Senate seat is key to Democrats’ hopes of winning back the upper chamber. It is also a major battleground state that has now voted for President Donald Trump in two of the last three presidential elections, even as it sends Democrats like Elissa Slotkin to the Senate. Michigan is now poised to become an early presidential nominating state , giving it outsized influence on the 2028 contest. Buttigieg laid out, in explicit terms, the broader stakes of a fractured Democratic coalition heading into the general election: “The stakes are high, and people from around the country, people from around the world, are watching the state of Michigan right now to see if we have the capability to put together that coalition to win.” “We're going to win because we know what it means to focus on what's at stake, to lock arms as allies after a spirited primary, to pull together in common cause,” said Buttigieg, who stayed neutral in the state’s Senate primary, at the Michigan Democratic Party’s general election kickoff rally. Abdul El-Sayed on Tuesday defeated Rep. Haley Stevens after a bruising primary that exposed ideological and demographic divisions within the party. He now faces Republican Rep. Mike Rogers in the general election, and he has to figure out how to pull moderate and establishment Democrats back into the fold to hold the seat. Republicans, seeing an opening with Black and Jewish voters who broke more for Stevens, are already trying to peel away parts of the Democratic coalition. They view Michigan as one of their best pickup opportunities this cycle. Buttigieg, who represents the party’s more moderate flank, used his remarks Friday to explicitly appeal to Democrats across the spectrum — and even some Republicans. “Wherever you sit, in this big tent of ours, and it is a big tent, but whatever corner of that tent you think of as home, there is a set of things, and I mean big, big things, where we agree with each other, we agree with most Michiganders, and Washington and Lansing Republicans disagree with us,” he said. “That's what's at stake right now, and it's not all about left, right, and center, Democrat and Republican.” Buttigieg’s remarks — and the early unification around El-Sayed in one of the nation’s most important battlegrounds — underscores the delicate balancing act party leaders have to contend with. After a string of progressive victories through the spring , establishment Democrats in particular are trying to rally behind their new nominees without necessarily embracing every part of the politics that carried them across the finish line. That dance showed up subtly throughout the speeches on Friday night. Buttigieg at one point framed El-Sayed’s position as wanting “to expand affordable health care and keep more money in your pocket,” whereas Rogers “voted against the Affordable Care Act.” Buttigieg notably did not use the phrase “Medicare for All” to address one of El-Sayed’s signature progressive positions. El-Sayed, for his part, also made an explicit effort to turn the page. “In the spirit of unity, in the spirit of the work, in the spirit of coming together, I want to thank both of my colleagues who ran, Haley Stevens and Mallory McMorrow, for an incredible race,” he said. “Their incredible public service in the state of Michigan, and I cannot wait to see what both of them will do next.” But he signaled that the progressive policy positions that powered his campaign would remain central to his general election stump. He reiterated his support for Medicare for All and railed against “the system of super PACs” and the millions of outside money flooding into politics. And he sharply criticized Rogers, who, along with his fellow Republicans, have dramatically increased their attacks against El-Sayed since he won the primary, offering an early glimpse of what is likely to be a combative and divisive general election. “They don't know who we fight for,” El-Sayed said. “We fight for the families barely able to put their groceries in the cart and check out, we fight for the mom who's worried about the child care she needs to be able to work a job that barely pays enough, we fight for the folks who are afraid about what happens if they get sick. We fight for each other, and we don't back down.”

"></img><p>Zohra Mohamed avanza tres pasos y retrocede seis. Está atrapada en la misma porción de la calle desde hace horas. Alguien le ha dicho que tras las rejas negras del edificio polifuncional de la barriada de El Príncipe puede haber esperanza, pero de momento no aparece. Tiene 62 años, 11 nietos y desde hace tres días, una más que no es de su sangre. Es Aya, de 17 años, una joven marroquí que cruzó a nado a Ceuta. Vestida con camiseta masculina, observa el diminuto ir y venir de Zohra, y repite su propio ritual nervioso, mordisqueando el colgante de una pequeña mariposa que lleva al cuello. “No abren, es que no abren aquí. Dime qué hago, dónde voy”, suplica Zohra a todo el que se cruza. Hace tres días vio a Aya en un callejón, con las piernas llenas de heridas y aún mojada por la travesía. Estaba sola, no tenía zapatos y era de noche. “¿Cómo iba a dejarla así? “Una niña sola, ¿cómo va a ser eso?”, repite agitada. Numerosos ceutíes han acogido a algunos de los miles de menores que el 30 y el 31 de julio entraron en Ceuta por el espigón fronterizo de El Tarajal, pero la solidaridad de los vecinos apenas da abasto para paliar la situación de estos jóvenes, y en especial la de las chicas, expuestas, además, a la violencia sexual.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-09/situacion-critica-de-las-menores-en-ceuta-violencia-sexual-y-refugiadas-con-sus-nuevas-madres.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

Fue en la sede nacional del PP, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-07-30/la-direccion-del-pp-se-pone-de-perfil-y-se-remite-a-las-explicaciones-de-ayuso-sobre-la-compra-del-atico-de-lujo.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-07-30/la-direccion-del-pp-se-pone-de-perfil-y-se-remite-a-las-explicaciones-de-ayuso-sobre-la-compra-del-atico-de-lujo.html">en una rueda de prensa de Miguel Tellado</a>. “Me remito a las explicaciones que han dado desde el Gobierno de la Comunidad”, contestó el secretario general de los populares. Tellado había dado la cara, aunque poniéndose de perfil, para salir al paso de la polémica cuando en Sol engordaron la bola mucho más en un lapso de tiempo ínfimo. Diez días después, la versión oficial del equipo de Alberto Núñez Feijóo sigue siendo la misma: remitirse a las palabras de la baronesa madrileña a pesar de que, cada día, la madeja <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/madrid/2026-08-04/el-gobierno-de-ayuso-pago-63-millones-por-el-atico-de-chamberi.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/madrid/2026-08-04/el-gobierno-de-ayuso-pago-63-millones-por-el-atico-de-chamberi.html">se enreda más con nuevas informaciones comprometedoras</a> . “Hay sensación de incomodidad innecesaria”, resume un parlamentario nacional. “Un lío innecesario”, añade.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-09/genova-da-un-paso-atras-en-la-polemica-del-atico-de-ayuso.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: (ACN) El Brunch Electronik Festival ha tancat l’edició del 2026 amb més de 70.000 assistents aquest cap de setmana al parc del Fòrum . L’esdeveniment de música electrònica ha acollit en tres jornades actuacions com les de The Blaze, Paul Kalkbrenner, CamelPhat, Luciano, Acid Arab o Max Dean. El festival també ha donat espai a projectes de diversos gèneres dins de l’electrònica com Lildami, Deborah de Luca, Cassius, AMÉMÉ y LP Giobbi, Wade, Âme DJ i Trikk, Jeff Mills o Miss Monique. En total, ha aplegat 28.000 persones en la primera jornada, 30.000 assistents en la segona i 8.000 més en la darrera. També et pot interessar 13 detinguts i 74 mòbils recuperats al dispositiu policial del Brunch Electronik Festival Neus Reig 1 minut de lectura l Brunch Electronik Festival va néixer fa quatre anys i s’ha consolidat com una de les cites més esperades per als amants d’aquest estil musical. En aquests tres dies, ha desplegat una programació que transita entre el  house, el tecno, l’electrònica melòdica  i els directes.
articles.headline: El Brunch Electronik Festival tanca l’edició 2026 amb més de 70.000 assistents en tres jornades

articles.body: L’ Europa ha guanyat 5 a 2 al Badalona i aconsegueix el segon Torneig d’Històrics del Futbol Català de la seva història. El conjunt dirigit per Josep Maria Gené ha fet una primera part excepcional amb gol de Flavio i doblet de Marc Anglès . A la segona meitat el Badalona ha retallat distàncies amb gols de Pepe Bonilla i Joaco , però Khalid ha sortit al rescat per sentenciar el partit. Amb aquesta victòria l’Europa tanca un Torneig d’Històrics amb molt bones sensacions. Encert de cara a porteria El partit ha començat de la millor manera pel conjunt escapulat. Marc Anglès ha inaugurat el marcador amb una rematada ajustada al pal dret, impossible pel porter del Badalona . Els de Gràcia no han afluixat i pocs minuts després, Flavio s’ha quedat sol davant del porter per fer el 2 a 0. El Badalona, tot i ser dos categories inferiors, ha plantat cara i ha fet lluir a Nil Ruiz , heroi a la tanda de penals davant el Sant Andreu . Abans d’anar al descans, Marc Anglès ha tornat a veure porteria amb un xut des de la frontal de l’àrea. Khalid sentencia el partit El Badalona ha retallat distàncies al segon temps amb gols de Pepe Bonilla i de Joaco de penal, però ha estat un miratge. L’Europa s’ha refet gràcies a Khalid que ha fet un doblet en el moment més important del partit. El davanter ha sentenciat el partit amb dos gols al tram final per donar el segon Trofeu d’Històrics del Futbol Català a l’Europa. articles.body: Aquest diumenge a la tarda la Guardia Urbana ha intervingut al rec Comtal de Vallbona després d’una sèrie de denuncies per una part del veïnat degut a l’ acumulació de brutícia a la zona. Els actes incívics dels banyistes han causat una situació de conflicte que ha culminat en l’arribada d’una desena de membres de la Guàrdia Urbana que ha desallotjat els banyistes que es trobaven al rec. El bany en aquest paratge natural va prohibir-se estrictament l’agost del 2021 , per tal d’evitar-ne l’ús lúdic i preservar-ne la biodiversitat i infraestructura històrica. Tot i les restriccions la presència de gent no ha afluixat. Aquest fet ha causat el descontentament del veïnat que no vol veure el rec amb les deixalles que alguns banyistes marxen sense recollir. “ Tota la vida ens hem remullat aquí , però és cert que últimament no s’està mantenint com toca, és una llàstima”. A més, alguns veïns han denunciat que la situació va a pitjor quan arriba la nit. “No podem descansar bé, posen música i fan molt soroll “, remarquen els veïns que viuen a la zona. També et pot interessar El rec Comtal s’activa contra l’incivisme i els banys Ruth Rodríguez Porta 3 minuts de lectura Més brutícia als entorns del rec Segons alguns veïns del barri que passen pel rec Comtal, aquest està cada cop més brut. “La gent deixa brutícia, no cuida els bancs i no ens hi podem seure “, així ho ha expressat un veí que freqüenta la zona. Alguns han observat que la gent que ve en grup és la que “pitjor ho deixa tot” . Tot i que els veïns lamenten aquesta degradació de l’espai, alguns banyistes defensen que banyar-se al rec Comtal és un costum arrelat a la zona i són conscients que cal recollir aquelles deixalles que hagin pogut generar al llarg de la jornada. Una activitat a l’abast de totes les butxaques Malgrat les restriccions i la prohibició de bany, moltes persones ho continuen veient com una bona opció perquè l’aigua d’aquesta sèquia mil·lenària és molt freda i els ajuda a passar calor en un barri on no hi ha cap piscina pública. “Venim aquí perquè és el que més ens podem permetre, ara mateix les piscines estan massa pujades de preu “, explica una banyista. Per a molts aquesta és l’opció més viable i assequible per combatre les altes temperatures , “amb aquesta calor que és massa forta venim a remullar-nos els peus i refrescar-nos una mica”, afirma una visitant recurrent. De fet, al barri de Vallbona no hi ha cap piscina pública . articles.body: Platges plenes a vessar : és la imatge típica d’un diumenge d’agost, quan a la sorra gairebé no hi cap ningú més. Però enguany, a causa de les altes temperatures, ni tan sols les meduses hi troben lloc . Els experts ho confirmen: no n’arriben tantes de mar obert i, a la costa, tampoc n’hi ha tantes de les que hi neixen. També et pot interessar Una altra calorada desmesurada, persistent i com a mínim per una setmana més Marcos Amores Sánchez 3 minuts de lectura Un mar massa calent L’absència de meduses pot semblar una bona notícia per als banyistes, ja que facilita el bany. Els experts, però, alerten que és un fenomen preocupant i el consideren un indicador més de l’impacte que les altes temperatures estan tenint sobre el mar . El principal motiu és la temperatura de l’aigua , excepcionalment alta aquest estiu. Les meduses que neixen a la costa podrien no haver superat les primeres fases de desenvolupament. Les que arriben de mar obert, com la Pelagia noctiluca , aquest any ho tenen més difícil per acostar-se al litoral, ja que l’aigua de la costa és molt més calenta. També et pot interessar A una dècima del rècord: 28,4 ºC al mar de la Barceloneta abans de l’aflorament d’aigües profundes Ariadna Corominas del Hoyo 2 minuts de lectura “Ni les meduses poden sobreviure” Segons Josep Maria Gili, biòleg expert en meduses de l’ICM, les meduses són una part habitual i necessària de l’ecosistema marí . “Fa 20 o 30 anys, una arribada massiva de meduses a la costa ja era un avís: el mar ens estava dient que l’estàvem alterant”. Ara, però, el missatge és encara més preocupant: l’escalfament de l’aigua és tan intens que “ni les meduses poden sobreviure” . Ho constaten també els banyistes. “Aquest any no n’he vist gaires. De fet, no n’he vist cap”, explica un usuari habitual del Centre Municipal de Vela, on practica pàdel surf, caiac i, ocasionalment, vela. articles.body: Paula Blasi ha aconseguit acabar en la cinquena posició del Tour de França , una fita extraordinària per a la ciclista d’Esplugues de Llobregat. Blasi, campiona de la volta ciclista a Espanya el mes de maig i de la Volta a Catalunya el juny passat , ha fet un Tour descomunal i la cinquena posició la porta a seure la mateixa taula que les millor corredores mundials del moment actual. No havia de córrer el Tour de França A començament de temporada Paula Blasi no va ser seleccionada pel seu equip, l’UAE, per participar en el Tour de França . La direcció del conjunt la contemplava com a una ciclista en formació i la tenia en una mena d’equip B. Però les circumstàncies van canviar durant la primavera . D’un dia per l’altre van dir-li que correria l’Amstel Gold Race i, per sorpresa de tothom, va guanyar-la . Després va venir el triomf a La Vuelta i a La Volta . La decisió de fer-la córrer al Tour podia semblar arriscada, però al final ha demostrat que estava capacitada per fer-ho. En el el seu debut a la prova francesa ha acabat cinquena, el que fa preveure que en pocs anys pot optar a guanyar-la. articles.body: El Sant Andreu ha fet oficial la incorporació de Pablo Agudín , que arriba cedit procedent del Reial Oviedo . Amb 18 anys, Agudín ja ha debutat amb el primer equip asturià i ha format part de les categories inferiors de la selecció espanyola. La temporada passada va disputar set partits a Primera Divisió, convertint-se en el cinquè jugador més jove de la història del club en debutar a la màxima categoria del futbol nacional. Més informació: https://t.co/wDCRxn7kh8 pic.twitter.com/ZjF95q9SPK — Unió Esportiva Sant Andreu (@uesantandreu) August 9, 2026 Debut contra l’Osasuna Pablo Agudín va debutar amb el Reial Oviedo el 4 de novembre del 2025 davant l’ Osasuna . Amb 17 anys, 11 mesos i 25 dies es va convertir en el cinquè jugador més jove de la història del club asturià en disputar un partit de La Lliga . Set partits va disputar la temporada passada a Primera Divisió, entre ells contra el Reial Madrid al Santiago Bernabéu. Va alternar convocatòries amb el primer equip i el filial, amb qui van acabar segons a la Segona Federació . Un reforç de luxe Es tracta d’un mitjapunta amb arribada. Amb el Reial Oviedo Vetusta va marcar tres gols en 19 partits a la Segona Federació . Amb el primer equip, no va ser capaç de veure porteria entre els 87 minuts repartits en set partits. L’objectiu de l’ Oviedo amb la cessió d’Agudín al Sant Andreu és que tingui minuts i sigui protagonista a la Primera Federació abans de fer el salt definitiu al futbol professional. articles.body: La  previsió  del temps  per a aquest dilluns, 10 d’agost, indica un temps marcat per la calor i la xafogor intensa. Tot i això, la temperatura baixarà un pèl respecte de diumenge. Temps canviant , amb més sol que núvols però sense descartar alguna nuvolada una mica més activa. Previsió horària per a Barcelona : 6 h: nit sufocant 9 h: sol i núvols 12 h: nuvolades passatgeres 15 h: més de 30 ºC 18 h: teranyines de núvols 21 h: núvols baixos i molta basca També et pot interessar Una altra calorada desmesurada, persistent i com a mínim per una setmana més Marcos Amores Sánchez 3 minuts de lectura Cel canviant i una mica menys de calor Dilluns de cel variable. Tot i que el sol s’imposarà durant molts trams del dia, entre el matí i el migdia aniran creuant bandes de núvols de sud-oest cap a nord-est que podrien amagar algun petit ruixat de curta durada. A la tarda els núvols seran més prims però n’apareixeran també de baixos a la costa, on augmentarà la humitat i la sensació de xafogor . Temperatures màximes una mica més baixes, sense que s’arribi als 35 ºC a la ciutat. Malgrat tot, es continuaran superant els 30 ºC de manera força general a Barcelona. Es mantindrà el temps bàsicament estable, però amb possibilitat de ruixats de tarda a muntanya i de núvols baixos a la costa , que podrien fins i tot dificultar veure amb netedat l’eclipsi total de sol d’aquest dimecres. La calor continuarà inamovible de dia i de nit , amb nits de molt mal dormir una darrere de l’altre i mínimes que difícilment baixaran dels 27 ºC al centre de la ciutat en tota la setmana. articles.body: El 12 d’agost és una data assenyalada al calendari des de fa mesos, especialment per a tots aquells que volen presenciar l’ eclipsi de sol . Ara bé, davant la temptació de voler-ne fer fotos o vídeos amb el mòbil , els experts adverteixen que serà millor deixar-ho als professionals o, en tot cas, utilitzar una càmera amb el filtre solar adient per no fer malbé la lent . I si posem un filtre a la lent del mòbil? És cert que amb el mateix filtre amb què ens protegirem els ulls podem protegir la lent dels mòbils —sempre i quan quedi completament coberta la càmera —. No obstant això, “tot i que estàs enfocant el sol, hi ha moments en què et tremolen les mans i el mòbil no el tapa del tot, de manera que la llum t’entra directament als ulls i podries patir danys a la retina”, explica l’astrònom Joan Anton Català Amigó. “En aquest cas, tu també hauries de portar unes ulleres homologades”, afegeix. Però assegura que, a la pràctica, això no té massa sentit: “Si tu et poses les ulleres no veus absolutament res, ni la pantalla del mòbil, ni el botó per a fer la fotografia. Aquesta és la raó per la qual desaconsellem que la gent intenti fer fotografies amb el mòbil .” A banda que, diu, amb aquests dispositius quedarien “ridículament petites”. També et pot interessar Eclipsi solar del 12 d’agost del 2026: horari i des d’on es veurà a Barcelona i Catalunya? Marcos Amores Sánchez 6 minuts de lectura Què canvia respecte quan mirem una posta de sol? Segons Català, no canvia res i, de fet, “ no hauríem de mirar mai una posta de sol de manera directa “. Ara bé, explica que en aquests casos el sol acostuma a anar molt baixet amb la qual cosa “l’atmosfera filtra la llum del sol i ens arriba més feble. Per això, no ens fa ferides a la retina de seguida”. Com diu, això també s’aplica a la càmera i fa que en una posta de sol puguem enfocar uns instants sense que passi res amb els nostres dispositius. Al cap i a la fi, “en una posta de sol acabem mirant el sol uns instants, no el mirem constantment, per això és tan important que amb l’eclipsi, tot i que estigui el sol baix, no es cometin excessos i que, encara que estigui molt baixet, no es pot mirar el sol 10 minuts”. Ni amb l’eclipsi, ni sense ell, conclou. articles.body: (ACN / Redacció) Els Mossos d’Esquadra investiguen un tiroteig després d’una baralla entre dos grups al barri de Verdum (Nou Barris), segons ha avançat El Caso i ha confirmat l’ACN de fonts policials. L’incident s’ha produït pels voltants de les 4.50 h de la matinada d’aquest diumenge al carrer d’Almansa i no consten ferits. Fugida dels atacants Segons les primeres informacions, la batussa entre els dos grups ha anat pujant de to fins que un dels integrants ha tret una arma de foc i ha efectuat diversos trets. Els participants de la baralla han fugit ràpidament deixant abandonats dos vehicles a la zona. Els Mossos han traslladat els turismes a dependències policials per analitzar-los i mirar de trobar alguna pista que ajudi a identificar els implicats en la trifulga. No hi ha constància de l’ingrés hospitalari de cap persona a conseqüència del tiroteig i la policia catalana tampoc no ha fet cap detenció. articles.body: Queden pocs dies perquè arrenqui la festa major de barri més antiga de la ciutat: la Festa Major de Sant Roc , al Gòtic. Per fer més entretinguda l’espera, des del 31 de juliol i fins al 12 d’agost , l’Associació de Festes de la Plaça Nova ens proposa la  ruta del panellet , un recorregut per diversos establiments del barri que té premi final: un panellet de Sant Roc, elaborat, avui, per la pastisseria La Colmena. També et pot interessar Festes de Sant Roc 2026 a Barcelona: del 12 al 16 d’agost a la plaça Nova i al barri de la Catedral Neus Valls 4 minuts de lectura Un dolç amb història Tot i que el nom pot fer pensar en els clàssics panellets de massapà, el panellet de Sant Roc és ben diferent, tant per la forma com pel gust. El seu origen està estretament lligat a la llegenda del sant i al seu gos. “És com una pasta de te una mica grossa i, sobretot, té gust d’anís. El gos de Sant Roc, el gos del forn, li regalava un pa cada dia i d’aquí ve el nom de panellet”, explica Laura Gómez, encarregada de la pastisseria La Colmena. És el quart any que La Colmena , un establiment centenari de Ciutat Vella, s’encarrega d’elaborar aquest dolç i de lliurar-lo als participants que completen la ruta del panellet. El negoci va recuperar-ne la recepta tradicional després que l’Associació de Festes de la Plaça Nova els proposés fer-se’n càrrec. “Quan ens ho van demanar ens va fer molta il·lusió. Vam fer unes quantes proves a partir de com recordàvem que era la pasta del panellet i finalment ho vam aconseguir”, assegura Gómez. També et pot interessar Pastisseria La Colmena, dolça com la mel Josep Maâti Salvat 2 minuts de lectura “Una manera de fer barri” Per participar en l’activitat només cal passar per La Casa dels Entremesos, recollir un passaport i ganes de recórrer alguns dels comerços del barri en busca de capgrossos plaçanovins . En total n’hi ha sis i estan amagats per diversos establiments de la zona. Segons l’organització, és una manera de divulgar la cultura i la tradició d’unes festes que venen des del 1589. “Parlem amb les botigues i és una manera també que el barri en si participi. A part de la gent del barri, i no del barri”, explica Miquel Àngel Gelabert, voluntari de l’Associació de Festes de la Plaça Nova.

articles.body: (ACN) L’Ajuntament de Barcelona ha habilitat a l’agost 19 de les 41 biblioteques que gestiona, cinc més que l’any passat, que se sumen a una xarxa de prop de 500 punts de refugis climàtics repartits per tot Barcelona. “Un parell d’hores al matí i un parell d’hores a la tarda, és essencial, sobretot en certes edats”, considera Phil Manzaneque, portaveu de l’Associació de Veïnes i Veïns d’Horta. També et pot interessar Refugi climàtic: per què al portal del bloc de pisos sempre s’hi està tan fresc a l’estiu? Ariadna Corominas del Hoyo 3 minuts de lectura La Biblioteca Can Mariner , al barri d’Horta, és un dels equipaments que tanca a l’agost tot i estar catalogat com a refugi climàtic. “Volem que aquesta biblioteca doni servei”, reclama Manzaneque. De fet, el portaveu proposa que el consistori obri més d’una biblioteca en cada districte durant el mes, com passa a Nou Barris, per exemple, on n’hi ha tres de disponibles. Iñaki Martínez (ACN) En el cas d’Horta, el centre cívic està tancat a l’agost i el centre esportiu només obre la sala de l’entrada, la qual cosa impossibilita fer estades llargues en aquest espai. També obre el casal de la gent gran, però que, per al portaveu, se centra en un tipus de veí molt concret. A la biblioteca, en canvi, “pots llegir el diari, pots veure una pel·lícula, pots consultar internet, no només per ser-hi, sinó perquè estiguis entretingut, per donar un servei”, assegura. Pelegrins climàtics a la García Márquez Una de les biblioteques de Barcelona obertes durant l’agost és la Gabriel García Márquez del districte de Sant Martí, que també dona servei els diumenges. De fet, aquesta biblioteca rep usuaris de molts barris de la ciutat, també de fora del districte. És el cas d’en Mauricio, que viu al Raval i veu impossible gaudir dels parcs amb la seva filla a l’agost. La biblioteca, en canvi, la tranquil·litza: “És un lloc agradable per ser-hi”.
